The canon of Scripture was handed down from the liturgical Tradition of the Church (East and West), and cannot be separated from that tradition. Martin Luther was the first one to attempt that separation with his sola scriptura heresy, and disaster quickly followed with everything from Calvin to the Anabaptists making up things to suit their own personal interpretations. Also, Luther removed books in his version of the Bible which were being used in the canon of his day and are still in the Catholic and Orthodox Bibles. So while the individual books of the Bible were Divinely inspired (think Divine Muse rather than automatic writing), the canon evolved over time.

A look back into the history of books used during the Liturgies of East and West will show lots of books which were used in centuries past, like the Shepherd of Hermas or Protoevangelion of James and are no longer used for that purpose. Generally the books which are part of the "apocrypha" are not part of the canon because they lack provenance: we either don't know who the author was, can't verify the information in the book, etc... The Didache is a great example of this, where tradition says it contains the teachings of the Apostles, but there's no hard evidence and so it isn't in the canon. This brings us to the book of Enoch: it's one of those books which was not included in the Hebrew Scriptures (Septuagint), and never had a history in the Orthodox or Catholic liturgies... however, the Ethiopian Coptic Church, which is an Apostolic Church not in union with Rome or the Orthodox, does have it in their canon. Not only that, but Enoch was never banned (nor was any of the "apocrypha") by the Eastern or Western Churches, and there are some really old copies out there IIRC. Protestant churches probably banned it though, because "muh sola scriptura".

The point of this is that it wasn't really "kept from the Bible" in any real sense, but should be taken with a grain of salt. Definitely a good read though, and makes one wonder what the ante-deluvian civilization got up to to make God wipe them out.
